Job Title: Lead Integrated Producer - Global HOKA

Reports to: Sr. Manager, Creative Operations & Production - Global

Location: US (Remote)


Interested applicants must reside in one of the following approved states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Indiana, Massachusetts,

Minnesota, New York, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Texas, Utah, Washington


The Role

As a Sr. Integrated Producer – Global HOKA, you’ll be a key member of the Operations and Production team, leading the end-to-end execution of integrated creative productions across the brand. You’ll collaborate with Creative, Project Management, Global Brand Integrated Marketing, and cross-functional partners to translate creative concepts into thoughtful production strategies. You’ll balance creative ambition, budget, timing, and business requirements, leading productions from creative development through pre-production, execution, post-production, and final delivery. This role primarily supports photography-led production but also includes video and motion content across campaigns.


We celebrate diversity--of your background, your experiences and your unique identity. We are committed to ensuring an inclusive and equitable workplace where all of our employees can Come as They Are. We believe that when we bring our different perspectives to work, we are truly Better Together.


Your Impact

  • Lead photo and video productions from creative development through to final delivery
  • Translate creative concepts into production strategies, scopes, schedules, and solutions
  • Serve as lead producer on assigned projects
  • Source, evaluate, negotiate, and manage production companies, photographers, directors, studios, post-production partners, and other vendors
  • Develop and manage production plans, budgets, bids, estimates, change orders, forecasts, and final reconciliations
  • Recommend production approaches and partners that maximize creative quality and production value within approved budgets
  • Administer talent, photographer, director, vendor, and other production-related agreements, including contracts, usage, licensing, and releases
  • Partner with Legal to ensure contracts and documentation reflect project scope, usage requirements, and financial commitments

description:
About The Role

Photographers are the eyes of the publication and we're looking for photographers who want to create the most iconic images of our era. We want photographers who's work that sit somewhere between documentation and fantasy. Your work should feel surreal, cinematic, raw, and unforced, and whether you shoot film or digital, in the studio or on the street, we want photographers who prioritize grit, mood, and instinct over commercial perfection.

Responsibilities

  • Cover nightlife, gallery openings, and cultural moments. We need editorial documentation, not commercial event recaps.

  • Translate creative direction and mood boards into final image sets that fit the publication’s aesthetic without losing your personal style.

  • Take charge of the environment and manage talent on set or on location to get the shot. You must be comfortable directing people, not just observing them.

  • Manage your own post-production to deliver high-resolution, editorial-grade files on deadline.

Requirements

  • 2+ years of professional experience in photography (editorial, portrait, or documentary).

  • You must have experience shooting portraits and human subjects. We are not looking for landscape or still-life specialists for this role.

  • Expert knowledge of manual camera settings, on-set lighting, and flash photography.

  • Proficient in Adobe Lightroom, Capture One, or Photoshop.

  • Your work has a defined style. We are not looking for standard commercial, bridal, or corporate event photography.

Compensation & Rates

This is a contributor-based role focused on editorial storytelling.

  • Editorial Stipends: We provide stipends for commissioned features and event coverage ($50–$100 USD per project depending on scope).

  • Expenses Covered: We cover entry fees, tickets, and production costs for assigned events and shoots.

  • Portfolio Growth: This role is designed for photographers looking to build a curated editorial portfolio with full creative credit and global visibility. Priority consideration is offered for future editorials and paid commissions as opportunities open.

Diversity & Inclusion

BLACKSTAR Haus is committed to a fair and inclusive hiring process and encourage applications from all backgrounds, regardless of location or previous industry access. We value the unique viewpoints that come from different lived experiences and prioritize creating a workspace where those voices are heard.

description:
Role Title: Photographer

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Northern America, Latin America, Europe, UK, Oceania.

micro1 is engaging Photographers to contribute their expertise to a video annotation project for a customer. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.

Scope of Work

  1. Review video footage of robotic arms performing a variety of tasks, ensuring careful observation of each session.
  2. Apply detailed video annotation and data labeling skills to tag and categorize footage according to specific grading guidelines provided by the project.
  3. Evaluate visual and photographic quality within the videos, applying photography principles to judge image clarity, composition, and relevance.
  4. Spot and document visual nuances, discrepancies, or issues in robot task execution, maintaining strict attention to detail at all times.
  5. Follow established project protocols and grading rules consistently for all assigned sessions to ensure exceptional data uniformity and reliability.
  6. Submit clear, accurate annotations and written observations through project tools and workflows.
  7. Collaborate asynchronously with trainers and project coordinators as needed to clarify guidelines or improve annotation quality.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Professional background in photography, with a keen eye for visual composition and technical image evaluation.
  2. Demonstrated experience in video annotation, data labeling, or related AI training projects, ideally involving robotics or technical footage.
  3. Exceptional attention to detail and an ability to spot subtle visual cues in dynamic environments.
  4. Strong adherence to complex guidelines and repetitive processes without sacrificing accuracy or quality.
  5. Experience using annotation platforms or visual data tools is highly desirable.
  6. Comfort working independently and managing deliverables in a remote, asynchronous project setting.
  7. Background knowledge in machine learning, robotics, or AI annotation projects is a plus but not required.
